diagnostics.message: kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config has an explicit depends_on on kubectl_manifest.aws_provider, but this ordering is already established transitively via time_sleep.wait_60_seconds (which itself depends_on kubectl_manifest.aws_provider). The direct depends_on entry is redundant.

kubectl_manifest.kubernetes_provider_config has an explicit depends_on on kubectl_manifest.kubernetes_provider, but this ordering is already established transitively via time_sleep.wait_60_seconds_kubernetes (which itself depends_on kubectl_manifest.kubernetes_provider). The direct depends_on entry is redundant.

kubectl_manifest.helm_provider_config has an explicit depends_on on kubectl_manifest.helm_provider, but this ordering is already established transitively via time_sleep.wait_60_seconds_helm (which itself depends_on kubectl_manifest.helm_provider). The direct depends_on entry is redundant.

kubectl_manifest.upbound_aws_provider_config has an explicit depends_on on kubectl_manifest.upbound_aws_provider, but this ordering is already established transitively via time_sleep.upbound_wait_60_seconds (which itself depends_on kubectl_manifest.upbound_aws_provider). The direct depends_on entry is redundant.

aws_eks_addon.adot depends (via the RoleVersion/ClusterRoleVersion tags hack) on the Kubernetes Role and ClusterRole for the eks:addon-manager principal, but not on the corresponding RoleBinding kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot. Without that binding the addon-manager has no permissions in the ADOT namespace, so the add-on can be installed before the RBAC prerequisites are in place and fail.

aws_eks_addon.adot depends (via the RoleVersion/ClusterRoleVersion tags hack) on the Kubernetes Role and ClusterRole for the eks:addon-manager principal, but not on the corresponding ClusterRoleBinding kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.adot. Without that cluster-level binding the addon-manager cannot create/update the ADOT CRDs, so the add-on can be installed before its RBAC prerequisites are in place and fail.
